criterion: M2 exit criterion 8 (ROADMAP.md): retro 3D flags, vertex snap and affine UVs, against CPU references on a committed mesh set
setup: web/world/retro3d.mjs draws textured triangles with a depth test into an RGBA8 target, with two flags. snap: each vertex's screen position is rounded to a grid of `snap` pixels before rasterising (the wobble of fixed-point vertex hardware). affine: UVs are interpolated linearly in screen space instead of perspective-correctly (the texture swim of hardware without perspective division). Texels are fetched nearest, with repeat. The CPU twin (retro3dRef) applies the same rules: pixel centres, a top-left fill rule, the same depth comparison. The committed mesh set is generated in code (web/world/retro3d_meshes.mjs): a cube, a floor of quads receding to the horizon (the case affine mapping visibly bends), and a cylinder, each drawn with each of the four flag settings.
metric: per pixel: coverage (which triangle, if any) and the fetched texel. A pixel is an edge pixel when any triangle edge passes within 1 pixel of its centre; there float rounding may legitimately decide coverage either way.

bounds.coverage: every pixel that is not an edge pixel has the same coverage on the GPU and in the twin
bounds.texels: at least 99.5% of pixels covered on both, away from edges, fetch the same texel; the rest differ by at most one texel in u or v (a UV landing within float precision of a texel boundary)

control: the affine scene compared with a perspective-correct twin, and the snapped scene with an unsnapped twin, must each fail the texel bound on the floor mesh
does_not_prove: That the look matches any particular console, colour depth reduction or dithering (those are the dither pass), or performance.

amended.date: 2026-10-10, after the first run, which failed the texel bound
amended.first_run: SwiftShader, twin with exact vertices: coverage matched in all 12 cases (0 mismatches away from edges), no texel was more than one away, and both controls failed; but the same-texel share was below 99.5% in 9 cases (0.849 to 0.991), all differences one texel.
diagnosis: Sub-pixel vertex precision: rasterizers snap vertex positions to a fixed-point grid whose size the APIs leave to the hardware (D3D12 requires 8 bits, Vulkan allows 4). Quantizing the twin's vertices to 1/16 pixel made every case with snap off exact (1/256 changed nothing), so SwiftShader uses 4 bits.

Exact texel ties: with snapped vertices on whole pixels, affine UVs are rational in the pixel position, so many samples land exactly on a texel boundary, where float rounding legitimately picks either neighbour. Every remaining mismatch was within 1/1000 texel of a boundary (cube 70 of 70, cylinder 358 of 358, floor all).
amended.change: The twin models the adapter's sub-pixel precision (subpixelBits: 4 for SwiftShader, 8 for D3D12 hardware), and samples within 1/1000 texel of a texel boundary are exempt from the texel bound, counted and reported, the same exemption the texture identity check (M2 criterion 3) uses. The coverage and texel bounds themselves are unchanged.
amended.basis: The coordinator's direction for M1 criterion 1 (2026-10-10): model the behaviour the APIs allow in the reference and keep the bound, recording a dated deviation. Applying it to this criterion is the engine session's inference, open to the coordinator's or the author's rejection.
